name: Yellowish umber
lede: Yellowish umber is a muted, olive-leaning brown carried into our library from a Japanese traditional color name, and it is one of the more common swatches in our painting archive.

sections.title: Iwaicha, an Iwai brown
sections.body:
Our library lists this color from the Wikipedia survey *Traditional colors of Japan*, under the romanized name Iwaicha, written 岩井茶 [1]. The library glosses the pair as "Iwai brown"; no further date or dyeing detail is given, and what "Iwai" itself refers to is undocumented here [1].

The nearest named colors on file are [[greyish-brownish-olive]], [[greyish-brownish-olive]] and [[guinea-hen]], at 3, 3 and 4.2 ΔE [1]. By the numbers, yellowish umber leans more yellow-green, at a hue angle of 86 degrees against umber's 56, while plain umber leans warmer and more orange [1]. The hex given here, #5E5545, is a modern screen reading chosen to match the library's gloss, not a measurement of dyed cloth or a pigment sample, so treat it as approximate [1].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body:
Our archive finds a color within range of this swatch in 5,763 of the 23,781 paintings we have, about 24 percent, as photographed[2]. It holds fairly steady across centuries, from roughly one painting in five to one in four, from the 1100s through the 1900s [2]. It turns up somewhat more in Korean and Chinese works than the archive average, at 1.77 and 1.4 times the expected rate [2].

Inside a painting it most often sits as a midtone, in 56 percent of the paintings that carry it [2]. It also plays a shadow role nearly a third of the time, in 31 percent, more often than it serves as a highlight, at 13 percent [2]. Measured values are screen approximations of varnished, photographed canvases, not a pigment identification [2].
